repair.title: Review SQLite transaction scope
repair.proposed_change: In _SandboxState.read_cached_source, release exclusive writer ownership before a separate read; keep critical sections short and add contention tests.
risks: Changing transaction boundaries can alter cache consistency.
verification: Capture concurrent local reads and confirm the measured lock behavior.

result.summary: All three incident /summary requests returned HTTP 500 with OperationalError 'database is locked'; the dominant failing span is cache.read (46-50 ms), while dependency.request succeeded (5-8 ms) and baselines were healthy. This points cautiously toward local SQLite contention rather than a dependency or schema fault, though the sample is tiny.

hypotheses.statement: Incident failures likely stem from local SQLite lock contention during the cache.read step: error spans are 'database is locked' and cache.read dominates failing latency, while the fixed loopback dependency stays ok.

supports.quote: error_type=OperationalError; message=summary failed: database is locked

alternatives: A concurrent writer holding a long transaction on the SQLite file could produce the same 'database is locked' text without the captured traces showing any writer span.
A stale or corrupt local cache file could raise OperationalError during cache.read, though the message wording favours locking rather than corruption.

uncertainty: Only one capture with three correlated incident requests and three baselines; not independent production samples, so rates cannot be inferred.
No writer, lock-holder or transaction span is captured, so contention is inferred from error text and span dominance rather than directly observed.
The baseline window contains no cache.read errors, so the change in behaviour is temporal correlation, not proof of a single root cause.
